summary: Water resources engineer and AIT master's researcher connecting hydrodynamic modelling, satellite Earth observation and machine learning to flood and drought risk. Experience spans Himalayan flood hazards, citizen science monitoring and reproducible basin-scale decision support, with ongoing research on satellite-informed Noah-MP correction and flash drought in Thailand.
projects: Developing satellite-informed correction of Noah-MP land surface model outputs for surface and root-zone soil moisture, terrestrial water storage, precipitation and evaporation. The research targets a 1 km gridded record for 1940-2025 and its application to flash drought in Thailand. Satellite observations inform correction over their available overlap; the full historical period is a model-based reconstruction.

Built basin-scale decision support for Thailand's 22 principal basins and national aggregate, integrating GRACE water storage, full-compartment groundwater estimates, climate reconstruction and observed groundwater comparisons. Includes 46 regional/target ensembles, independent temporal testing and evidence from 511 wells. Residuals retain model and observation uncertainty and do not establish pumping volumes.
HydroEVT | Nepal Hydrological Extreme Flow DSS

Co-developed HydroEVT and its Streamlit decision-support interface for Nepalese flood and low-flow frequency analysis. The workflow combines observed-record quality checks, stationarity and independence diagnostics, L-moment distribution fitting, goodness-of-fit ranking, return-period design flows and bootstrap uncertainty. Interactive station and catchment views communicate record quality and uncertainty alongside the estimates.

Co-authored Beyond a flash flood, an AIT technical report reconstructing the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli disaster. The study integrates climate and seismic records, satellite imagery, field observations and RAMMS-HEC-RAS modelling to examine a cascading rock-ice avalanche and downstream flood disaster, with recommendations for multi-hazard early warning and transboundary preparedness.
RAMMS | HEC-RAS 2D | ERA5-Land | Satellite analysis | Multi-hazard risk
Co-authored dam-break research using HEC-RAS to examine downstream flood hazards and potential consequences in Kathmandu, Nepal.
Developed and evaluated an LSTM model for multi-step streamflow forecasting, with hydro-meteorological time-series preparation and comparison against conventional forecasting methods.
Analysed soil moisture, precipitation and terrestrial water storage indicators using SMAP, ERA5 and GRACE, with Python processing and drought severity mapping for Nepal's Terai region.

Prepared a term report on landslide susceptibility and building exposure in Bagmati Province, Nepal. Compared SE-DenseNet, TabTransformer and XGBoost using a landslide inventory and 13 environmental factors at 30 m resolution; combined susceptibility maps through spatial ensemble analysis and used SAM-based building detection in high-risk areas. Included case studies of the 2014 Jure and 2024 Jhyaple Khola landslides.
GeoAI | SE-DenseNet | TabTransformer | XGBoost | SAM | Spatial ensemble
Compared multiple linear regression, Ridge, Lasso and Elastic Net for fire prediction in the Bezia region, using cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning to address model selection and overfitting.
Nan River basin flood forecasting, Thailand

Developing an integrated deep learning and hydraulic modelling framework for the Nan River basin. The proposed chain couples LSTM temporal learning with directed graph neural network routing for seven-day discharge forecasts, HEC-RAS 2D reference simulations and a ConvLSTM surrogate for flood depth, velocity and inundation extent. Planned evaluation uses RID discharge, TMD meteorology and Sentinel-1 flood observations, with a daily-updatable web decision-support prototype. Model skill and operational performance remain to be established.
LSTM-GNN | HEC-RAS 2D | ConvLSTM | Sentinel-1 | Flood DSS

Co-authored QUAL2K and MODFLOW group reports with Mohammed Yameen and Farzeen Khan. The QUAL2K project examined dissolved oxygen, CBOD loading and interventions including weirs and riparian shading. The MODFLOW project compared steady-state groundwater heads, water balances and wetland discharge under alternative boundary conditions and pumping scenarios.
QUAL2K | MODFLOW | Dissolved oxygen | Groundwater flow | Scenario analysis
Completed a term report applying the HBV rainfall-runoff model.
